subject: Request: Latency attribution & observability evidence for private deployment
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@borealtech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya.lin@borealtech.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment latency — what evidence do you need for an SLA carve?

Hi Logan,

We're running Redwood Private inside our VPC (single-tenant, customer-managed network) and over the last month we've seen several short, high-p90/p99 latency spikes that correlate with scheduled batch jobs on our side. Our legal and procurement teams have asked what the process is to document a shared-responsibility exception so these spikes don't count toward Redwood uptime SLOs.

What specific observability artifacts do you require from our side (packet captures, tcptrace, NTP logs, firewall session dumps, application traces) versus what Redwood can provide from the private agent? Also, is there a standard appendix or language you prefer for the SLA that distinguishes customer-network-caused latency from Redwood runtime issues?

We need to prepare something to present to our CFO and procurement early next week — any checklist would help.

Thanks,
Sam Ortiz
VP of Ops
Boreal Technologies

[Attachment: customer-sample-spike-notes.txt (text)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@borealtech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency — what evidence do you need for an SLA carve?

Sam —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answer: we can scope an operational appendix that attributes latency events to customer-controlled network/infra when the root cause is demonstrably outside the Redwood agent runtime. To make that robust for legal/procurement we typically ask for a small set of artifacts from the customer side plus some traces we produce from the agent.

Checklist we usually request:
- Customer-side: packet-level PCAP for the window, network device logs (firewall, load balancer), and cron/job schedule notes if there are correlated batches.
- Timing sync: NTP/chrony logs around the event so timestamps align.
- Redwood-side: agent-side per-request latency histograms, KV cache hit/miss logs, and a short otel trace covering request->response.

Irene (CC) will be the technical lead on gathering and correlating traces. Naomi (CC) will draft the shared-responsibility appendix language we propose to Procurement/Legal.

One quick note: for privacy/compliance reasons we avoid full packet payloads in shared documents; metadata and headers are usually enough. We'll accept masked PCAPs if you need to redact.

I'll share a template appendix and the specific fields we need from the agent. Can you confirm whether you can pull PCAPs and NTP logs for the windows you observed?

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Link: https://app.redwood.com/docs/private-sla-observability#evidence]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@borealtech.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency — what evidence do you need for an SLA carve?

Hi Sam / Logan —

We ran a capture of the agent-side telemetry for the windows you mentioned and correlated it with the job schedule you shared. Attached are: edge-latency-trace-1120.zip (agent histograms + otel spans) and vpc-topology-1120.pdf (simple diagram showing where the agent lives in your network and the firewall hops). Initial observations: during the 2027-11-03 02:00–02:15 UTC spike, the agent saw a steady increase in TCP retransmits between your LB and the agent host; agent-side CPU and KV cache hit-rate remained normal, which points toward a network-induced tail latency rather than a runtime stall inside the model process.

I've included inline excerpts below for context.

On Sat, 20 Nov 2027 at 09:12 AM, Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@borealtech.com> wrote:
> We're running Redwood Private inside our VPC (single-tenant, customer-managed network) and over the last month we've seen several short, high-p90/p99 latency spikes that correlate with scheduled batch jobs on our side.

What we recommend next if you want an SLA appendix:
- Provide the PCAP fragment (or redacted metadata) for the event window.
- Allow Redwood to produce a short joint incident note demonstrating correlation (we can timestamp-align using your NTP logs).
- Agree on attribution thresholds (e.g., >50% packet loss or >200ms additional RTT attributable to customer network in the event window) in the appendix.

I'll leave the appendix language to Naomi, but technically we've collected the telemetry you asked for. If you'd like, we can run a controlled scaled load test during your maintenance window to show the difference between baseline and your scheduled batch run.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Technical Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: edge-latency-trace-1120.zip (zip), vpc-topology-1120.pdf (pdf)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@borealtech.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency — what evidence do you need for an SLA carve?

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the quick collaboration and for providing the initial schedule and traces. Based on Irene's telemetry and your confirmation we can draft a short Shared Responsibility Appendix (SRA) that:

- Defines observable conditions for network-attributed latency (examples: retransmit rate threshold, delta RTT over baseline, verified firewall queueing window).
- Lists the evidentiary artifacts both sides will produce and the retention period for each (we recommend 90 days for traces attached to SLA disputes).
- Outlines an operational playbook for joint investigations and the escalation path back to Redwood support and Boreal OPS.

I've attached a first-pass SRA draft (sra-draft-boreal-1123.docx). Key commercial asks for Procurement: we propose a simple exception clause that excludes short, network-attributed p99 spikes from uptime breach calculations provided both evidentiary conditions are met. This will need legal sign-off; if you can loop Procurement/Legal I can push a DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.com/REQ-8932-Boreal
Evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBorealEvidence

If this aligns, please reply with the procurement contact and a preferred SLA threshold (we typically see customers choose either a delta-RTT threshold (+200ms) or a packet-retransmit threshold (>5% over baseline) — happy to include both as options in the appendix.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sra-draft-boreal-1123.docx (docx)]
